description: Manifest of env vars required by a HealthLog production deployment. Used by `pnpm check-env` to catch missing/empty vars BEFORE a deploy ships. v1.4.42 W6 — born out of the v1.4.40 AP-2 .p8 install gap that shipped silently for 3 days.

groups.name: Core
groups.description: Database, app URL, encryption keys. The app refuses to boot without these.

variables.name: DATABASE_URL
variables.purpose: Postgres connection string. App boot fails if missing.

variables.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
variables.purpose: Database password for the bundled `db` service in docker-compose.yml.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
variables.purpose: Public URL embedded in OAuth redirects, webhook callbacks, APNs deep-links.

variables.name: APP_URL
variables.purpose: Server-side mirror of NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL; used by background workers.

variables.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
variables.purpose: AES-256-GCM key for at-rest encryption of provider tokens. 64 hex chars (32 bytes). Required unless ENCRYPTION_KEYS is set.

variables.name: API_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY
variables.purpose: HMAC-SHA256 key for hashing external Bearer tokens AND web session cookies. 64 hex chars. Rotating it signs every browser session out on top of invalidating every issued token.

groups.name: Withings OAuth
groups.description: Withings API credentials are entered per user in Settings → Integrations (no env-var path). Only the webhook shared secret is operator-level.

variables.name: WITHINGS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
variables.purpose: Random secret carried as a path segment in the Withings webhook callback URL. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`.

groups.name: Polar OAuth
groups.description: Required to enable the Polar AccessLink integration. App boots without these but the Polar connect button stays disabled. Register an app at https://admin.polaraccesslink.com and set the redirect URI to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/api/polar/callback.

variables.name: POLAR_CLIENT_ID
variables.purpose: Polar AccessLink OAuth client id.

variables.name: POLAR_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.purpose: Polar AccessLink OAuth client secret.

groups.name: Oura OAuth
groups.description: Required to enable the Oura Cloud v2 integration. App boots without these but the Oura connect button stays disabled. Register an app at https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/applications and set the redirect URI to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/api/oura/callback.

variables.name: OURA_CLIENT_ID
variables.purpose: Oura Cloud OAuth client id.

variables.name: OURA_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.purpose: Oura Cloud OAuth client secret.

groups.name: OIDC SSO login
groups.description: Required to enable SSO login against a self-hosted identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, Google Workspace, etc.). App boots without these but the login page's SSO button stays hidden. Register a confidential client with redirect URI ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/api/auth/oidc/callback.

variables.name: OIDC_ISSUER_URL
variables.purpose: OIDC provider issuer URL (discovery doc served at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration).

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.purpose: OIDC confidential client id.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.purpose: OIDC confidential client secret.

groups.name: OIDC SSO options
groups.description: Optional tuning for an enabled OIDC provider. Each stands alone (deliberately NOT allOrNone — any subset is valid) and each has a safe default when unset.

variables.name: OIDC_SCOPES
variables.purpose: Space-separated scopes requested at authorization. Default: "openid email profile".

variables.name: OIDC_BUTTON_LABEL
variables.purpose: Label on the login page's SSO button. Default: "Single Sign-On".

variables.name: OIDC_ONLY
variables.purpose: "true" disables password/passkey login server-side (only effective when the OIDC provider group is fully configured). Default: additive login. Locks the native iOS app out of sign-in.

groups.name: AI Provider
groups.description: Optional runtime policy and output tuning for user-configured AI providers. Each variable stands alone and has a safe default when unset.

variables.name: AI_PRIVATE_ORIGINS
variables.purpose: AI endpoints on the operator's own network (Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM). Comma-separated exact origins (scheme://host[:port]), e.g. "http://ollama.lan:11434". Unset, a private AI base URL is refused (apart from what the deprecated ALLOW_LOCAL_AI_PRIVATE_HOSTS=true still covers). Link-local, metadata and unspecified addresses stay refused even when listed; a malformed entry is logged once and grants nothing.

variables.name: ALLOW_LOCAL_AI_PRIVATE_HOSTS
variables.purpose: Older form of AI_PRIVATE_ORIGINS, kept for existing installs: an exact comma-separated host list still grants those hosts. "true" is deprecated since v1.39.3: it covers only the admin AI key and AI settings saved on an admin account (pinned; metadata and link-local refused), is reported at boot and on the admin AI settings page, and will be removed in a later release.

variables.name: INSIGHTS_MAX_TOKENS
variables.purpose: Daily-briefing output-token ceiling. Default 2500, clamped to 500-8000.

variables.name: INSIGHTS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR
variables.purpose: Per-user hourly ceiling for POST /api/insights/generate. Default 10; values below 1 fall back to the default.

variables.name: DOCUMENT_AI_LIMIT_PER_HOUR
variables.purpose: Per-user hourly ceiling for the document-AI actions (read/index, extract, suggest, summarise share one bucket). Default 6, clamped to 1-1000.

variables.name: AI_SYNC_REGEN_GAP_HOURS
variables.purpose: Minimum hours between two status-card regenerations after a sync. Default 6, whole hours 1-48; hand entries keep one hour. The admin AI setting wins.

variables.name: DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_LIMIT_PER_HOUR
variables.purpose: Hourly upload ceiling per document-upload token (Paperless workflow, import script). Default 120, clamped to 1-1000. Web and phone uploads keep their own bucket.

variables.name: LABS_OCR_LIMIT_PER_HOUR
variables.purpose: Per-user hourly ceiling for lab-report scans (photo/PDF and browser-OCR text share one bucket). Default 6, clamped to 1-1000.

groups.name: Offline geolocation
groups.description: Optional offline GeoLite2 tier for the admin login overview. Unset, the runtime reads /opt/geolite2 (the path the image bakes its own copy into) and falls back to the online provider when the databases are absent.

variables.name: GEOLITE2_DIR
variables.purpose: Directory holding GeoLite2-City.mmdb + GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb. Point it at a read-only mount to bring your own databases. Default /opt/geolite2.

variables.name: MAXMIND_LICENSE_KEY
variables.purpose: MaxMind licence key for the runtime GeoLite2 fetch (issue #659). Set it and the worker downloads both databases into GEOLITE2_DIR on boot and monthly, no rebuild or manual mount. Free at maxmind.com/en/geolite2/signup.

groups.name: Outbound requests
groups.description: Switches for the requests HealthLog makes to third parties on its own. All default to on; set any of them to 1, true or yes to turn that request off.

variables.name: IP_GEO_LOOKUP_DISABLED
variables.purpose: Stops the online IP-to-location lookup for login events and the monthly MaxMind download. Only the local GeoLite2 databases are used.

variables.name: PASSWORD_BREACH_CHECK_DISABLED
variables.purpose: Stops the HaveIBeenPwned range query made when a password is set. The query carries the first five hex characters of the password's SHA-1, never the password or the full hash.

variables.name: UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED
variables.purpose: Stops the daily request to the GitHub releases API behind the About page and the admin version tile.

groups.name: Environmental context (Open-Meteo)
groups.description: Endpoints and switches for the opt-in Environment module. Every variable is optional: unset uses the hosted, keyless Open-Meteo services. Point the URLs at a self-hosted Open-Meteo instance to keep coordinate lookups off a third party.

variables.name: OPENMETEO_BASE_URL
variables.purpose: Historical weather (archive) API base URL. Default https://archive-api.open-meteo.com.

variables.name: OPENMETEO_GEOCODING_URL
variables.purpose: Geocoding API base URL for the home and travel location search. Default https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com.

variables.name: OPENMETEO_AIR_QUALITY_URL
variables.purpose: Air-quality API base URL (CAMS air quality, pollen, UV). Default https://air-quality-api.open-meteo.com. CAMS data is licensed by the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service; the attribution is shown in the app.

variables.name: ENVIRONMENT_AIR_QUALITY_DISABLED
variables.purpose: Set to 1, true or yes to stop the air-quality requests for the whole instance. Weather and daylight keep working; the per-user switch cannot turn air quality back on.

groups.name: Database session tuning
groups.description: Per-session Postgres settings the app applies to every pooled connection.

variables.name: DATABASE_WORK_MEM
variables.purpose: Postgres work_mem for every app session, as a Postgres size string. Default 16MB. Raise it when large sorts and aggregates spill to disk; each sort step of each connection may use this much.

variables.name: DATABASE_SESSION_OPTIONS_DISABLED
variables.purpose: Set to 1, true or yes to send no session settings (statement timeout, work_mem) as the libpq options startup parameter. Needed behind PgBouncer, which refuses that parameter unless it is in ignore_startup_parameters.

groups.name: APNs (iOS push)
groups.description: All four core APNS_* vars together. Missing any disables APNs silently — the v1.4.40 AP-2 gap that motivated this manifest. allOrNone trips the synthetic <all-or-none> required row whenever 1-3 of the 4 are set.

variables.name: APNS_KEY_ID
variables.purpose: 10-char Key ID from Apple Developer.

variables.name: APNS_TEAM_ID
variables.purpose: 10-char Team ID from Apple Developer.

variables.name: APNS_BUNDLE_ID
variables.purpose: iOS app bundle id, e.g. dev.healthlog.ios.

variables.name: APNS_KEY
variables.purpose: APNs auth key (.p8 contents). Use APNS_KEY for 12-factor env-block deploys; APNS_KEY_FILE is the filesystem alternative — at least one of the two must be set.

groups.name: Deploy webhook
groups.description: Coolify -> HealthLog deploy-result webhook. Without this, the auto-deploy success/failure feedback loop is broken.

variables.name: DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
variables.purpose: Shared secret of POST /api/internal/deploy-webhook. 64 hex chars. A request authenticates by sending it in the X-Deploy-Webhook-Secret header (Coolify's stock sender; no replay protection), or by signing: X-Deploy-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 under this secret of the X-Deploy-Webhook-Timestamp value, a dot and the raw body>, the timestamp within 5 minutes.

variables.name: DEPLOY_LOGS_URL
variables.purpose: URL of the deployment dashboard (e.g. the Coolify UI) linked in deploy-failure notifications. Optional; when unset the notification omits the link.

variables.name: DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_TIMESTAMP
variables.purpose: "true" (or "1") requires a fresh X-Deploy-Webhook-Timestamp (within 5 minutes) on a deploy-webhook request that authenticates with the secret header; one without it is refused with 401. Keeps a stale capture out, not a fresh forgery by someone who saw the secret. Leave unset for Coolify's stock sender, which sends no timestamp.

variables.name: DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE
variables.purpose: "true" (or "1") accepts only signed deploy-webhook requests (X-Deploy-Webhook-Signature with a fresh X-Deploy-Webhook-Timestamp); the secret header alone is refused with 401. The setting that stops a replay. Leave unset for Coolify's stock sender, which can only send the secret header.

groups.name: TLS leaf pin monitor
groups.description: Baseline for the TLS leaf SPKI-change alarm. The native client pins the served leaf certificate; without this the monitor logs the served pin but cannot alarm on a rotation. See docs/ops/tls-cert-pin.md.

variables.name: TLS_LEAF_SPKI_PINS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated known-good leaf SPKI pins, base64(sha256(DER subjectPublicKeyInfo)) — the same value the native client pins. Hold both the current and the next pin during a dual-pin renewal window.

groups.name: SMTP (email channel)
groups.description: Operator SMTP transport for the email notification channel (v1.17.1). All of SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_FROM together enable the channel; SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS are optional (unauthenticated relay). Missing any of the three core vars disables email silently — the channel is never offered and the Settings card hides itself.

variables.name: SMTP_HOST
variables.purpose: SMTP server hostname, e.g. smtp.example.com.

variables.name: SMTP_PORT
variables.purpose: SMTP port. 587 for STARTTLS (SMTP_SECURE unset/false), 465 for implicit TLS (SMTP_SECURE=true).

variables.name: SMTP_FROM
variables.purpose: From address for outbound mail, e.g. "HealthLog <noreply@example.com>".

groups.name: Notification targets on a private network
groups.description: Operator grant for webhook (Gotify, Home Assistant, n8n) and ntfy targets on the operator's own network. Unset, a target that resolves to a private address is refused at send time and the test button reports private_origin_not_approved. Optional; public targets never need it.

variables.name: NOTIFICATION_PRIVATE_ORIGINS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated exact origins (scheme://host[:port], no path, no wildcard, no CIDR), e.g. "https://gotify.example.com,http://ntfy.lan:8080". Link-local, metadata and unspecified addresses stay refused even when listed; a malformed entry is logged once and grants nothing.

groups.name: Dawarich on a private network
groups.description: Operator grant for Dawarich instances on the operator's own network, read by the movement context of the Environment module. Unset, a Dawarich URL that resolves to a private address is refused at connect time with private_origin_not_approved. Optional; a public instance never needs it.

variables.name: DAWARICH_PRIVATE_ORIGINS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated exact origins (scheme://host[:port], no path, no wildcard, no CIDR), e.g. "http://dawarich.lan:3000". Link-local, metadata and unspecified addresses stay refused even when listed; a malformed entry makes the connect form name it.

groups.name: Document picker
groups.description: Operator grant for the document picker, which lets a person search their own Paperless-ngx or Papra instance and import picked documents. Unset, the picker is off. Optional.

variables.name: DOCUMENT_SOURCE_ORIGINS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated exact origins (scheme://host[:port], no path, no wildcard, no CIDR), e.g. "https://paperless.example.com,http://papra.lan:1221". Only listed origins are contacted, public or private; redirects are not followed; link-local, metadata and unspecified addresses stay refused even when listed; a malformed entry is logged once and grants nothing.

groups.name: Off-host backups
groups.description: Required ALL-OR-NONE: any of these without the rest disables backups silently.

variables.name: BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT
variables.purpose: S3-compatible endpoint URL.

variables.name: BACKUP_S3_BUCKET
variables.purpose: Bucket name.

variables.name: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY
variables.purpose: S3 access key.

variables.name: BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY
variables.purpose: S3 secret key.

variables.name: BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY
variables.purpose: Separate AES key for the backup body — MUST NOT match ENCRYPTION_KEY.

groups.name: Database dumps
groups.description: The nightly whole-database dump and the dump before migrations (docs/ops/disaster-recovery.md). Optional: each has a default, and the bundled compose file mounts the `backups` volume at the default directory.

variables.name: DB_BACKUP_ENABLED
variables.purpose: Set false to stop the nightly database dump. On when unset.

variables.name: DB_BACKUP_DIR
variables.purpose: Directory the dumps are written to and restored from. Default /var/lib/healthlog/backups, the `backups` volume. In a container it must be a mount of its own: a directory in the container's layer is lost at the next update and counts as none. Without one the nightly dump only goes off-host and no dump is taken before migrations.

variables.name: DB_BACKUP_SCHEDULE
variables.purpose: Five-field cron for the nightly dump, in Europe/Berlin time like every scheduled job. Default 30 1 * * * (01:30).

variables.name: DB_BACKUP_KEEP
variables.purpose: How many nightly dumps stay in DB_BACKUP_DIR (default 7, at least 1). The last two dumps taken before a migration are kept besides.

variables.name: DB_BACKUP_BEFORE_MIGRATE
variables.purpose: Set false to start without the dump the entrypoint takes before applying migrations. On when unset; a failed dump stops the start until it works or this is false.

groups.name: Operational windows and cookie flags
groups.description: Values the product states back to a user or that decide whether a session cookie is accepted. Optional: each has a documented default. They are listed so `pnpm check-env` reports them, and so the compose whitelist and the example files can be held in step with this manifest.

variables.name: AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS
variables.purpose: How long audit rows survive, in days (365 by default). Published, not merely enforced: the shared-access activity feed and the dialog that ends somebody's access both state the number back to the user.

variables.name: ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS
variables.purpose: Days an account deletion, a managed-profile deletion or a data wipe stays undoable before the purge erases it (14 by default, 30 at most, 0 erases immediately). The account is locked at once. Published: the deletion dialogs and the Data & Privacy page state the number.

variables.name: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE
variables.purpose: Forces the Secure flag on every cookie the app issues. Unset, it tracks NODE_ENV. Set false for a LAN / VPN-only self-host served over plain HTTP, where the default makes login look broken.

variables.name: HEALTHLOG_PLATFORM
variables.purpose: Where this server's environment is configured (compose, truenas, coolify, unraid, portainer). Shown back to the admin: the "Back up your encryption key" step opens on that platform's instructions. Unset means compose.

variables.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY_CHECK
variables.purpose: The start-up encryption key check. enforce (default) refuses to serve when the configured key does not open the stored data; warn only logs the finding, names it as a warning on /api/health, serves anyway and records no key until the check passes. A last resort for a refusal the operator is certain is false; it disables a safety check.

variables.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS
variables.purpose: Trusted reverse-proxy hop count; the client IP is read that many entries from the right of X-Forwarded-For. Forwarding headers are read only from a peer whose own address is not public (loopback, private, CGNAT, unique-local, link-local, reserved, multicast).

variables.name: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated CIDRs (IPv4 or IPv6; a bare address is one host) the reverse proxy connects from. Set, only a connection from inside them may report the client address in X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP; every other connection is its own client. Unset, any non-public address may, which behind Docker Desktop, OrbStack or docker-proxy includes every caller of a published port. Same host: 127.0.0.1/32,::1/128; Docker network: the proxy's subnet. An entry that is not a CIDR lets no connection report an address and is named at boot.

variables.name: TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP
variables.purpose: "1" takes the client IP from Cloudflare's CF-Connecting-IP header, from every connection and before the peer check. Safe only when the origin accepts connections from Cloudflare alone (a Tunnel, or a firewall admitting only Cloudflare's ranges); otherwise any caller forges the address rate limits and the audit log record. Off by default.

variables.name: BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_PREVIOUS_KEYS
variables.purpose: Comma-separated off-host backup keys that are no longer written with but may still be needed to read older objects. Set during a rotation of BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY until the bucket's lifecycle rule has retired every object written under the old key.

variables.name: BACKUP_MAX_STORED_MB
variables.purpose: Largest stored backup of one account the app keeps, in megabytes of encrypted copy (2048 by default). A storage limit, independent of the app's memory: a backup past it fails with a message naming this variable, and the previous copy stays.

groups.name: Heap diagnostics
groups.description: Opt-in heap snapshot for chasing an out-of-memory crash. Off by default; a snapshot holds decrypted health data and keys. See docs/ops/heap-diagnostics.md.

variables.name: HEALTHLOG_HEAP_SNAPSHOT
variables.purpose: Set to 1 to write one heap snapshot the first time the heap reaches 85 % of its limit.

variables.name: HEALTHLOG_DIAG_DIR
variables.purpose: Directory the heap snapshot is written to. Default /tmp.
